builds.name: Reference: Ranked bot core
builds.goal: Reference for Kalista: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ bot players use most (22,080 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 55% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A mobile attack-stacking marksman who builds Rend spears while hopping and coordinates with an Oathsworn ally. Resetting Rend on a kill permits repeated pressure. The current adc provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Statikk Shiv → Guinsoo's Rageblade → Terminus. Lethal Tempo keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Gluttonous Greaves, Guardian Angel, Blade of The Ruined King.
builds.summary: The proven bot baseline: Statikk Shiv → Guinsoo's Rageblade → Terminus, with Lethal Tempo.
testPlan: Play it in bot as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Statikk Shiv → Guinsoo's Rageblade → Terminus) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 55% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Statikk Shiv → Guinsoo's Rageblade → Terminus.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula: Kalista puts her Oathsworn into Stasis and draws them to herself for up to 4 seconds. The Oathsworn can click to launch themselves, stopping at the first champion hit and Knocking Back all nearby enemies. If the Oathsworn hits a champion, they are placed at their maximum attack range from it.

Passive: When Kalista and her Oathsworn both Attack the same target, she deals [(0.1 / 0.12 / 0.14 / 0.16 / 0.18) × 100]% max Health magic damage. This effect has a [10] second Cooldown per target and a cap of [100 / 125 / 150 / 175 / 200] to non-champions.

Active: Kalista sends a ghost to patrol an area for three laps. Champions spotted are revealed for 4 seconds. This ability has 2 charges ([90 / 80 / 70 / 60 / 50] second refresh).

Kalista hurls a spear, dealing [10 / 75 / 140 / 205 / 270 + (1.05) × AD] physical damage to the first target hit. If this kills the target, the spear continues onward, carrying any {{Spell_KalistaExpungeWrapper_Name}} stacks to the next target hit.

Kalista can dash after using this Ability using {{Spell_KalistaPassiveBuff_Name}}.

Passive: Kalista's spears linger in their target for 4 seconds, stacking any number of times.

Active: Kalista rips the spears from nearby enemies, dealing [5 / 15 / 25 / 35 / 45 + (0.7) × AD + (0.65) × AP] plus [7 / 14 / 21 / 28 / 35 + (0.2 / 0.275 / 0.35 / 0.425 / 0.5) × AD + (0.5) × AP] physical damage per spear beyond the first. Slows enemies hit by [0.1 / 0.18 / 0.26 / 0.34 / 0.42 + (0.0005) × AP] for [2] seconds.

If this Ability kills at least one target, its Cooldown is refreshed and it refunds [10 / 15 / 20 / 25 / 30] Mana.

builds.name: AP Rend accumulator
builds.summary: Test ap rend accumulator against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test ap rend accumulator against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Rend has a 0.65 AP initial term and 0.5 AP per additional spear, despite dealing physical damage. Nashor creates separate magic attack damage while AP grows the spear cash-out; Terminus covers both damage types without buying magic penetration for Rend itself.
testPlan: Required state: Accumulate real spears within their four-second persistence window.
Compare Rend at three, six and ten recorded spears.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Slows reduce kiting and low AD weakens attacks before enough spears stick.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Rageblade phantom hits are not assumed to create extra Rend spears.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Guinsoo's Rageblade, Terminus, Rabadon's Deathcap, Banshee's Veil, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Critical duel
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Kalista: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A mobile attack-stacking marksman who builds Rend spears while hopping and coordinates with an Oathsworn ally. Resetting Rend on a kill permits repeated pressure. Fix Rend spear count and hopping/attack effectiveness. Multi-target bolts may help but must be tested; Oathsworn coordination and actual reset kills matter. Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows.
builds.summary: Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Kalista: Fix Rend spear count and hopping/attack effectiveness. Multi-target bolts may help but must be tested; Oathsworn coordination and actual reset kills matter.

Start with the early core (Kraken, then Navori if attack-driven recycling works) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Throw a fast moving spear that passes through enemies it kills. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: A Lifeline slot excludes Sterak/Maw; melee access or ranged spacing must be earned.

The route fails Kalista's stated kit question: Fix Rend spear count and hopping/attack effectiveness. Multi-target bolts may help but must be tested; Oathsworn coordination and actual reset kills matter.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: A Lifeline slot excludes Sterak/Maw; melee access or ranged spacing must be earned.
Full cost 16,550 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Kraken, then Navori if attack-driven recycling works. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Infinity Edge, Immortal Shieldbow, Lord Dominik's Regards are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Pierce transfer execution
builds.summary: Test pierce transfer execution against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test pierce transfer execution against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Pierce deals 1.05 total AD physical damage and transfers stored spears only when it kills the first target; Shojin supports Q/E spell trades while Cleaver helps repeated physical cash-outs; Death's Dance protects the exit. Earned Muramana supports poke but the route sacrifices normal attack speed.
testPlan: Required state: Prepare a killable minion carrying measured spears in front of the champion.
Measure transfer success and E reset on champion versus minion kills.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: A surviving first target blocks the transfer and leaves weak sustained attacks.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: No spear transfer through a target that survives Q, and R requires an Oathsworn. Black Cleaver and Last Whisper upgrades cannot be combined.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Muramana, Spear of Shojin, Black Cleaver, Death's Dance, Edge of Night, Ionian Boots of Lucidity. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
